speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin the assessment of this newborn, could you please describe the specific physical examination findings and any relevant history provided?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: What specific physical examination findings are present on the newborn? Please describe any skin lesions, respiratory distress, or other abnormalities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a continuous heart murmur (patent ductus arteriosus), chorioretinitis (cloudy lenses), and sensorineural hearing loss is classic for congenital syphilis, not cellulitis. REQUEST TEST: VDRL or RPR for syphilis serology.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic triad of symptoms, a negative initial VDRL may be a false negative or require confirmation with more specific treponemal tests. REQUEST TEST: Treponemal specific antibodies (FTA-ABS or TP-PA).

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative syphilis serology despite classic signs points to another TORCH infection, likely Congenital Cytomegalovirus. REQUEST TEST: CMV PCR on urine or saliva.

speaker: Doctor
text: With negative syphilis and CMV results, I suspect Congenital Rubella Syndrome given the patent ductus arteriosus, cataracts, and deafness. REQUEST TEST: Rubella IgM antibodies.
